paper_metadata.title: Performance Comparison of QAOA Mixers for Ternary Portfolio Optimization

summary: This paper studies gate-based QAOA for ternary portfolio optimization on DAX30 data, using 2 qubits per asset and comparing five mixers: Standard, XY Ring, XY Parity Ring, XY Full, and QAMPA. For N=5 (10 qubits) and N=8 (16 qubits), the noiseless simulator results favor XY Full and QAMPA, but under depolarizing noise the Standard Mixer overtakes the XY variants at very small noise levels (e.g., eta = 0.003 at p=1 for approximation ratio, and eta = 0.005 at p=1 for optimal probability).

experiments.description: QAOA portfolio optimization on a ternary (long/flat/short) DAX30 portfolio with N=5 assets and B=2, comparing five mixers on statevector and QASM simulation.

algorithm.variant: QAOA with Standard Mixer, XY Ring Mixer, XY Parity Ring Mixer, XY Full Mixer, and QAMPA
algorithm.ansatz: problem unitary + mixer unitary alternating layers
algorithm.parameter_initialization: For p=1, grid search over initial parameters; for p>1, four estimation methods based on prior layer p-1 parameters, selecting the one minimizing the objective

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Two qubits per asset: x_i^- and x_i^+ with z_i = x_i^+ - x_i^-; total register size 2N qubits
problem_formulation.objective_function: min_z F(z)= q * sum_{i,j} sigma_ij z_i z_j - (1-q) * sum_i mu_i z_i, subject to sum_i z_i = B; with penalty F^(A)(z)=F(z)+A(sum_i z_i-B)^2 for Standard Mixer only
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: XY mixers enforce feasibility via hard constraint-preserving subspace and Dicke-state initial state; Standard Mixer uses penalty term
problem_formulation.problem_hamiltonian: F-hat obtained by substituting z_i -> (Z_i^- - Z_i^+)/2; cost unitary includes pairwise ZZ terms and single-qubit Z terms

problem_instance.description: Ternary portfolio optimization on real DAX30 stock data

dataset_specification.preprocessing: daily adjusted closing prices -> daily simple returns -> annualized expected returns and covariance matrix

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Missing data dropped; daily simple returns computed; expected returns annualized via geometric compounding with 252 trading days/year; covariance matrix estimated from daily returns and annualized by multiplying by 252
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: 20 randomly generated portfolios; average approximation ratio and optimal solution probability over the 20 instances; statevector and QASM simulations compared

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Portfolio data from Yahoo Finance; return/covariance estimation; penalty coefficient A chosen so infeasible solutions are not favored
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Measure output distributions; compute approximation ratio and optimal solution probability

speedup_claims.caveats: No classical runtime or asymptotic speedup comparison is reported; the paper compares mixer performance within QAOA only.

complexity_analysis.quantum_complexity: QAOA is a gate-based variational algorithm; no asymptotic complexity claim specific to this paper

advantage_assessment.crossover_size: No crossover size reported; only N=5 is studied in the noiseless and QASM simulations.
advantage_assessment.resources_for_advantage: No quantum advantage resources are demonstrated; the best result is a noiseless simulator comparison where XY Full and QAMPA outperform the Standard Mixer on approximation ratio and optimal-solution probability.
limiting_factors: No classical solver benchmark against the quantum outputs
Performance depends strongly on mixer choice and noise

hardware.type inferred as simulator_other because the paper uses Qiskit Statevector Simulator and Qasm Simulator, with no real QPU.
circuit_depth not explicitly given as a single total depth; p values are reported instead, so depth is left null in resources and p is captured in num_layers.

experiments.description: Noise-robustness study of QAOA for the ternary portfolio optimization problem on N=5 assets and B=2 under depolarizing noise, comparing the same five mixers across p=1,3,5,7.

algorithm.variant: QAOA with Standard Mixer, XY Ring Mixer, XY Parity Ring Mixer, XY Full Mixer, and QAMPA under depolarizing noise
algorithm.ansatz: problem unitary + mixer unitary alternating layers with depolarizing channel after every one-qubit and two-qubit gate

key_results: The paper reports crossover noise thresholds where the Standard Mixer outperforms the XY mixers: for approximation ratio r, eta = 0.003 (p=1), 0.001 (p=3), 0.0005 (p=5), 0.0005 (p=7).
For optimal solution probability P, the crossover thresholds are eta = 0.005 (p=1), 0.003 (p=3), 0.001 (p=5), 0.001 (p=7).
The paper concludes that XY mixers are superior in noiseless settings, but the Standard Mixer becomes better beyond modest noise due to larger gate overhead and fragile Dicke-state initialization.
